summary: Shared durable-consumer contract checks: distinguish durable deletion, validate envelope type against subject
description:
TKT-99's broker-level test asserts the exact waitConsume diagnostic, but that message covers every async termination ("durable deleted or subscription terminated"). The test therefore proves deletion happened and that something terminated the consume context — not that the first caused the second. jetstream distinguishes them (ErrConsumerDeleted, pull.go:722); access does not surface it. Fix is a production diagnostic/readiness-surface change, so it was split out of the test-only ticket.

---

## Absorbed TKT-133 — inventory never validates the envelope `type` against the subject

Inventory's catalog consumer dispatches purely on the NATS subject
(`knownSchemas[msg.Subject()]`, `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:201`) and ignores
`type` entirely. Access checks it in both consumers (`consumer.go:360`, `policy.go:96`).
Pre-existing at `origin/main`; TKT-126 preserved the behaviour deliberately and recorded the
asymmetry in ADR-033 rather than silently fixing it.

ADR-009 §5 makes `type == subject` part of the envelope contract, so inventory currently accepts
envelopes that violate it. And TKT-126 introduced an inconsistency, deliberately and with a test
(`TestDecodeEnvelopeRejectsNonStringType`): a **non-string** `type` fails the shared decode and
terminates, while a **wrong-string** `type` is accepted — disposition depends on the JSON
representation of the same contract violation.

Sub-scope:
- [ ] Inventory validates `env.Type` against `msg.Subject()` before schema dispatch, **or** the
      decision not to is recorded with a reason (the broker, not the payload, may be the deliberate
      routing authority)
- [ ] Missing / mismatched / non-string `type` reach the **same** disposition class, not three
- [ ] Consumer-level tests pin the chosen behaviour for all three shapes, at a known and a future
      schema, asserting the exact action sequence and the readiness outcome
- [ ] ADR-033's "what deliberately does not live here" section and the `domainevent` package doc match

## Why these are one ticket

Both belong to `shared/go/durableconsumer` — TKT-133's own text says the `id`/`type` checks belong in
the skeleton, and TKT-127 (which built it) is now **Done**, so this is where they land. TKT-123's
diagnostic moved there too when TKT-127 lifted `waitConsume`
(`shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go:83`), which means fixing it once now covers access *and*
inventory instead of only access as originally scoped.

Both halves are the same question asked at two layers: **what does this consumer actually verify
before it acts, and can it tell you which thing went wrong?** One plan gate.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Split out of TKT-99's ai-review as an incidental finding (R4, medium) — real, but its fix is a
production change that a test-only ticket had no business making.

**The finding.** TKT-99's smoke test proves durable deletion terminates the access consumer by
asserting the exact diagnostic access writes:

> `access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)`

That message is produced by `consumer.waitConsume` for *any* async termination. So the test proves
(a) we deleted the durable and (b) *something* terminated the consume context — not that (a) caused
(b). A coincident NATS connection or subscription failure inside the 15s window would satisfy both
counters even if durable deletion had stopped closing `ConsumeContext.Closed()` entirely. The
strongest form of the test is currently unreachable from outside the process.

**Why it is small in practice, and still worth closing.** The window is 15s, the smoke stack is a
single-node hermetic broker, and a broker failure would break the rest of the suite loudly. But the
test's whole value is causal, and it is one indistinguishable log line away from being decorative.

**Shape of the fix.** `waitConsume` receives only a closed channel, so it cannot name the cause.
`jetstream` exposes it: `ErrConsumerDeleted` is what `pull.go:722` treats as terminal. Surfacing
the terminal error — via the consume error handler, or by having the caller record the last
terminal error alongside the latch — would let both the log line and the test say *deleted*
specifically. That is a change to ADR-017's readiness/termination surface and to a diagnostic
operators read, so it wants its own plan and its own review.

**Also worth deciding in the same ticket:** whether the two `waitConsume` callers should report
distinguishable reasons at all, or whether "terminated, and here is the underlying error" is
enough. TKT-97 deliberately kept the message coarse; this is a revisit of that call, not a bug in it.

Code pointers: `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go` (`waitConsume`),
`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:212`, `consumer.go:429`,
`smoke/access_consumer_test.go` (`policyTermination`, the assertion that would tighten).
Governing ADR: ADR-017 §5b (§236-241).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — TKT-123
**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** per `config.models.plan`, briefed with TKT-122's constraints (the
diagnostic is a contract asserted in two places; `Wait` now returns nil on the ambiguous case).
Verbatim below; critique in `kind=plan-final`.

---

### Draft plan — TKT-123

**Decision** — Amend ADR-034 and ADR-033 first, then implement two independent changes in one PR:

1. Capture broker-confirmed durable deletion and report it through the shared lifecycle helper.
2. Make inventory enforce the envelope’s `type == subject` contract.

Do not move JetStream registration or service disposition into shared code; ADR-034 leaves handler registration service-owned (`docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md:130`), while the shared package owns termination reporting (`docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md:144`).

### Half A design

Add a zero-value `durableconsumer.TerminationCause` backed by an atomic enum. Each `Run` creates one per consume context and registers:

```go
jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler(func(_ jetstream.ConsumeContext, err error) {
    if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConsumerDeleted) {
        cause.MarkConsumerDeleted()
    }
})
```

Pass that cause to `waitConsume`/`Wait`. The callback remains service wiring; classification state and diagnostic formatting live in `shared/go/durableconsumer`.

Use an atomic, not a channel or `atomic.Pointer[error]`: the callback must never block, only one stable classification is required, and sequentially consistent store/load supplies cross-goroutine visibility. In nats.go v1.52, the error handler runs before the subscription is stopped and `Closed()` becomes ready, so receiving `Closed()` after deletion observes the preceding atomic store.

All three currently optionless calls must register the handler: access issuer (`services/access/internal/consumer/consumer.go:429`), access policy (`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:189`), and inventory (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:522`).

Literal diagnostics:

```text
%s: consume context closed (durable deleted)
%s: consume context closed (subscription terminated)
```

Smoke expects:

```text
access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted)
```

Arbitration:

- A captured deletion wins even if cancellation and `Closed()` are also ready. It is genuine broker evidence, not the ambiguous shutdown-caused closure TKT-122 protects against.
- Without a captured deletion, cancellation continues to win deterministically and returns `nil`, preserving `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go:71`.
- Do not wait after cancellation for a cause that has not yet arrived; that late race remains the accepted no-join residual.

Move both contract assertions deliberately: the shared exact literal at `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait_test.go:113` and the smoke literal at `smoke/access_consumer_test.go:36`. The smoke should assert the narrower message because it explicitly deletes the durable at `smoke/access_consumer_test.go:279`. Add a second shared exact test for the generic subscription-termination fallback.

### Half B design

Validate. ADR-009 makes equality contractual (`docs/adr/ADR-009-contract-first-apis.md:46`); treating the broker subject as routing authority does not justify accepting a contradictory envelope.

Inventory disposition for missing, mismatched, or non-string `type`:

```text
actions == ["term"]
readiness remains true
no quarantine, provision, or other store mutation
```

That matches inventory’s poison vocabulary. Do not copy access’s failure-publication policy:

- Access order detects mismatch at `services/access/internal/consumer/consumer.go:360`, records `invalid_contract` (`consumer.go:367`), then terminates with that reason after successful failure publication (`consumer.go:341`).
- Access policy terminates directly with `invalid_contract` (`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:96`, `policy.go:100`).

Place the inventory check after `DecodeEnvelope`, known-subject resolution, and broken-schema handling, alongside the stable `id` check, but before `env.Schema > spec.max` (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:218`, `consumer.go:244`):

```text
read stable envelope
→ establish that the broker subject is owned
→ validate stable envelope invariants: schema, id, type == subject
→ dispatch schema range
→ decode and validate data
```

This preserves the load-bearing question order documented at `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:202`: the check examines stable envelope metadata only and never decodes future `data`. ADR-017 already classifies wrong `type` as poison alongside missing `id` (`docs/adr/ADR-017-domain-event-schema-evolution.md:228`).

Update ADR-033’s deliberately-service-owned checks (`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md:168`) and the matching package documentation (`shared/go/domainevent/envelope.go:28`). Do not add subject-aware validation to `DecodeEnvelope`; it has no broker subject and deliberately stops at universal readability (`shared/go/domainevent/envelope.go:139`).

### Open decisions

1. **Cause location:** shared `TerminationCause`, instantiated per service consume context; atomic enum for non-blocking, visible cross-goroutine publication.
2. **Ownership:** capture/reporting primitive in `durableconsumer`; `ConsumeErrHandler` registration remains in each service.
3. **Messages:** exactly the two literals above; durable name remains the prefix.
4. **Assertions:** update `wait_test.go:113` and `smoke/access_consumer_test.go:36` together; smoke asserts deletion-specific text.
5. **Validate or not:** validate and `Term()` as inventory poison, readiness untouched.
6. **Type-check ownership:** inventory, not `domainevent` or `durableconsumer`; shared packages document the contract/boundary only.
7. **Relationship:** two changes in one PR, not one abstraction. They share only the gate, documentation amendments, and one touched inventory file.

The validation is honest-writer contract consistency, not security or tamper-evidence: a broker-capable adversary can publish matching forged subject/type values (`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md:220`).

### Test seam

**Half A:** `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait_test.go` pins cause visibility, both exact messages, readiness, and both arbitration cases. `smoke/access_consumer_test.go` is the causal seam: removing the real handler registration makes deletion fall back to the generic diagnostic and fails the verbatim assertion.

**Half B:** `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go` drives `Consumer.handle` through `fakeMsg`, whose exact action recorder and `Term()` are at `consumer_test.go:27` and `consumer_test.go:50`. It fails if a known violation provisions, a future violation quarantines, readiness changes, or more than one disposition occurs.

### Test plan

Red-first after the ADR amendments:

1. Change the smoke literal and add shared tests for deletion-specific, generic, known-cause-over-cancellation, and ambiguous-shutdown cases.
2. Add six hand-written inventory JSON cases: missing, wrong-string, and non-string `type`, each at known schema 2 and future schema 5.
3. Assert exact `["term"]`, readiness true, and empty mutation/quarantine records for every case.
4. Implement shared capture/arbitration and wire all three consumers.
5. Implement the inventory check and synchronize ADR/package comments.
6. Run focused Go tests, then `make check`; the gate includes smoke (`Makefile:17`).

### DoD

- Half A distinguishes broker-confirmed deletion from generic termination.
- TKT-122’s shutdown preference remains for cause-less closures; confirmed deletion is the documented exception.
- Both literal assertion sites change together and the smoke proves the narrower cause.
- Inventory validates `type == subject`.
- Missing, mismatched, and non-string forms all terminate without readiness or persistence effects, at known and future schemas.
- Tests use hand-written JSON; no fixtures are marshalled from `domainevent` types.
- ADR-033, ADR-034, and both package comments reflect the final ownership boundary.
- `make check` passes.

### Files

- `docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md`
- `docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md`
- `shared/go/domainevent/envelope.go`
- `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go`
- `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait_test.go`
- `services/access/internal/consumer/consumer.go`
- `services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go`
- `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go`
- `services/access/internal/consumer/run_test.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/envelope_tolerance_test.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run.go`
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go`
- `smoke/access_consumer_test.go`

### Risks / Cons

- Correct classification relies on nats.go’s handler-before-`Closed()` ordering; the real-broker smoke is the regression proof.
- Only `ErrConsumerDeleted` becomes specific; other terminal errors remain generic.
- A real deletion concurrent with shutdown will now log and fail instead of being suppressed. That is intentional because the captured cause removes the ambiguity.
- Inventory becomes stricter for wrong-string `type`; previously accepted retained messages of that shape will terminate.

### Migrations / schema / wire

No database migration, OpenAPI regeneration, domain-event schema bump, or event-wire change. The operator diagnostic string is an intentional observable-contract change.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan-final — TKT-123 (delta on the `kind=plan` draft)

**Critique by `main-agent`** (`config.models.planReview`). **The `kind=plan` draft as amended below
is the plan.** Gate 2 waived; decisions mine.

---

#### The two load-bearing claims, verified in source rather than accepted

**1. The `ConsumeErrHandler` fires BEFORE `Closed()` becomes ready.** The whole design rests on this
— an atomic stored by the handler must be visible to a `Wait` that then observes `Closed()`. The
draft asserted it about a third-party library; TKT-122 is a fresh reminder of what happens when such
a claim goes unchecked. **Verified at `nats.go@v1.52.0/jetstream/pull.go:277-280`:**

```go
if sub.consumeOpts.ErrHandler != nil {
    sub.consumeOpts.ErrHandler(sub, termErr)
}
sub.Stop()          // Stop is what eventually closes Closed()
```

Handler first, `Stop()` second. **Claim holds.** Pin this ordering in a comment where the atomic is
read, because it is a dependency on library internals that a nats.go upgrade could silently break.

**2. The smoke literal.** Confirmed: `smoke/access_consumer_test.go:35-37` deletes
`access-slot-policy` and asserts the full string **including the `access: ` service prefix**. New
expected value:
`access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted)`.

#### Decisions

**D1 — ACCEPT the shared `TerminationCause` (atomic enum), with registration staying in each
service.** Correct split per ADR-034: the package owns *"when a consumer stops and what it says about
it"*; handler registration is wiring. An atomic over a channel is right — the callback must never
block, and only one stable classification is needed.

**D2 — ACCEPT the arbitration exception, and state precisely why it does not reopen TKT-122.**
This is the amendment most likely to be wrong, so the reasoning is explicit:
TKT-122 made shutdown win because **`Closed()` does not encode its cause** and this process closes
subscriptions itself (`defer nc.Close()`, no join). A captured `ErrConsumerDeleted` is a **server
status message** (409 Consumer Deleted, `pull.go:719-723`) — `nc.Close()` cannot produce it. So the
exception is scoped exactly to the evidence TKT-122 lacked, and it introduces no false-alarm path:
the ambiguous case still returns `nil`.
**Hard rule, from the draft and kept:** never *wait* after cancellation for a cause that has not yet
arrived. That late race stays the accepted no-join residual.

**D3 — ACCEPT half B: validate, `Term()`, beside the existing `id` check.** I reached the same
placement independently before reading the draft. It sits in inventory's broken-envelope branch
alongside `env.ID == uuid.Nil`, which already cites ADR-009 §5 for exactly this reasoning — stable
envelope fields whose absence is poison even when `schema` claims the future. Same disposition, same
readiness treatment, question order preserved (stable metadata only; `data` never decoded).

The three shapes then land in **one** disposition class, which is sub-item 2:
| shape | path | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| non-string `type` | `json.Unmarshal` fails → step 1 | `Term`, readiness untouched |
| missing `type` | `"" != subject` → new check | `Term`, readiness untouched |
| mismatched `type` | new check | `Term`, readiness untouched |

**D4 — AMEND the file list.** The draft lists `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go` but the
same threading is needed in **`services/inventory/internal/consumer/run.go`** — both services wrap
`durableconsumer.Wait` in a local `waitConsume`, and both signatures change.

**D5 — REJECT any claim that this is a security control.** The draft says so already and it is right:
validating `type == subject` is **honest-writer contract consistency**. Anyone who can publish to the
subject can publish a matching forged `type`. ADR-021's rule — say which adversary you mean — applies
to the ADR wording too.

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model
1. **The verified library-ordering claim (and the requirement to comment it at the read site).**
2. **D4's addition of inventory's `run.go`.**

#### Reasoning lens — pre-mortem
- *"Your deletion exception reopened the false-alarm path TKT-122 closed."* → **D2**: scoped to a
  server status message `nc.Close()` cannot generate.
- *"A nats.go upgrade reordered the handler and your atomic reads stale."* → comment the dependency
  at the read site; the shared test pins the observable behaviour.
- *"You changed a contract string and one of the two assertion sites still passed."* → both move
  together, and the smoke asserts the **narrower** message, which it can because it deletes a durable.

#### Test seams
- **Half A** — `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait_test.go`: both literals, both arbitration cases
  (captured-deletion-beats-cancellation, ambiguous-still-nil), readiness. `smoke/access_consumer_test.go`
  is the causal seam: without handler registration, deletion falls back to the generic message and
  the verbatim assertion fails.
- **Half B** — `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go` via `fakeMsg`'s action
  recorder: six **hand-written JSON** cases (missing / wrong-string / non-string × known schema 2 and
  future schema 5), asserting exactly `["term"]`, readiness unchanged, no store mutation.

#### DoD
Deletion is distinguishable from generic termination · TKT-122's shutdown preference survives for
cause-less closures · both literal sites move together and smoke proves the narrower cause ·
inventory validates `type == subject` · all three shapes reach one disposition at known and future
schemas · hand-written fixtures only · ADR-033/034 and both package docs match · `make check` green.

#### Files (draft's list + inventory's `run.go` per D4)
`shared/go/durableconsumer/{wait.go,wait_test.go}` · `shared/go/domainevent/envelope.go` (doc) ·
`services/access/internal/consumer/{consumer.go,policy.go,run.go}` ·
`services/inventory/internal/consumer/{consumer.go,run.go,consumer_test.go}` ·
`smoke/access_consumer_test.go` · `docs/adr/ADR-033-*.md` · `docs/adr/ADR-034-*.md`.
**Migrations: none. Wire/schema: none.**

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Coding — TKT-123

**Implemented by `main-agent`** per `config.models.implement`. PR
[#133](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/133) · branch
`TKT-123-consumer-contract-checks` · one commit.

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent
commit: ac1f84e
gate: make check — EXIT=0, log body clean; TestAccessDurableDeletionTerminatesAndRecovers PASS
ci: none (no Actions minutes); local gate is sole gate; branch protection off (403)
generated_drift: none
migrations: none
wire/schema: none
```

#### TDD

| Test | Red evidence |
|---|---|
| `TestTypeMismatchIsPoisonWhateverItsShape` | 4 of 6 rows red; the two non-string rows already passed **correctly** (decode error → `Term`) and stand as regression guards that the three shapes stay converged |
| `TestWaitDiagnosticNamesTheConfirmedCause` | the literal did not exist |
| `TestConfirmedDeletionOutranksShutdownButAmbiguityDoesNot` | `broker-confirmed deletion must survive a concurrent shutdown, got <nil>` |

**The known-schema rows were rewritten before implementing.** With empty `data` they terminated on
*payload validation* rather than the contract, so they passed against the defect. Giving them valid
payloads means the only thing between those envelopes and a successful provision is the `type` check.
Same trap as TKT-116/117 — a red test that is red for the wrong reason.

#### The moment this could have gone very wrong
Adding the `type` check failed **27 existing subtests**. The tempting conclusion is "fixtures are
stale". But those fixtures omit `type` because nothing ever required it — and if **catalog** also
omitted it, the same check would have terminated *every real event in production*, not 27 fixtures.

I verified `services/catalog/internal/events/events.go` sets `Type: SubjectPerformancePublished`
before touching a single fixture. It does. The fixtures are pre-contract artifacts and the check is
safe. Had that grep gone the other way, this ticket would have stopped for the human.

Fixtures are stamped with their subject's `type` at the `fakeMsg` sites (`withSubjectType`) rather
than edited literal-by-literal: `type` is not those tests' variable, and the one test where it *is*
deliberately does not use the helper. One quarantine assertion compares against the **delivered**
bytes rather than the bare literal, since the property under test is "quarantine stores what
arrived".

#### An implementation error the tests caught
My first version put the confirmed-cause exception only in `Wait`'s `ctx.Done()` arm. With both arms
ready Go picks at random, so a pick of the `closed` arm still preferred shutdown and **swallowed the
confirmed deletion**. Both arms now honour it. Caught by the arbitration test, not by reading.

#### Deviations from `kind=plan-final`
One the plan should have listed: the **fixture sweep**. `quality-practices.md` §1 warns that changing
a disposition breaks fixtures riding the old one (TKT-74's lesson) — the plan named the ADR/doc
updates and the new tests, but not the 27 existing subtests. Everything else went as decided, including
D4's addition of inventory's `run.go`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### AI review — TKT-123

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex `adversarial-review`, primed for guilt, diff only), per
`config.models.aiReview`. Cross-model invariant holds.

**Verdict: `approve`, no material findings. One pass.**

> *"nats.go v1.52 invokes ErrHandler before Stop for terminal 409 deletion status (pull.go:270-280);
> clean Stop/Close does not manufacture ErrConsumerDeleted. The atomic and escaped cause remain
> race-safe, inventory validates only stable envelope fields before schema dispatch, and all catalog
> producers for published/archived/closed/reopened — including festival and seated variants — set
> type correctly. The two live diagnostic assertions agree."*

#### Why one pass, and why that is not a shortcut
The skill's second pass exists to review **the fix diff** — code no reviewer has seen. Nothing was
found, so nothing was fixed, so there is no such diff. One pass, recorded as the deliberate call it
is. This is the first ticket of the run where that has been true.

#### Agreement between two independent checks
Every load-bearing fact in this diff was verified by me before the review ran, and the review reached
the same answers by its own route:

| Claim | My check | Reviewer |
|---|---|---|
| `ErrHandler` fires before `Stop()` | `pull.go:277-280` | `pull.go:270-280` ✓ |
| A clean stop cannot forge `ErrConsumerDeleted` | 409 is a server status message | ✓ |
| Every producer sets `type` | `events.go:313/420/361` — 4 subjects | ✓ **and** festival + seated variants |
| Type check does not break ADR-017's ordering | stable fields only, `data` never decoded | ✓ |
| Both diagnostic literals agree | shared test + smoke | ✓ |

The producer check is the one that mattered most and where the reviewer went **further than I did**:
I verified the four subjects `knownSchemas` keys on; it also confirmed the festival and seated
variants of those payloads. Had any producer omitted `type`, this diff would have terminated real
events rather than 27 fixtures.

#### Findings I raised against myself, before the review
- **The 27-fixture sweep and the production question underneath it.** Verified catalog emits `type`

### retro:

**(1) What would have made this ticket faster or better?**

- **The plan missed the fixture sweep, and `quality-practices.md` §1 already warns about exactly
  this.** It says: *when a plan changes a disposition, sweep every suite for fixtures riding the old
  one* (TKT-74's lesson). My plan-final listed the ADR updates, the new tests and the file list —
  and not the 27 existing subtests that would break. The rule was there; I did not apply it.
  **Concrete change: none to the skill.** This is a case of an existing rule not being followed, not
  a missing rule. Worth naming as such rather than patching a document that already said it.
- **Verifying my own riskiest claims before review paid for itself, measurably.** Three self-found
  defects (single-arm arbitration, vacuous known-schema rows, the un-stamped quarantine comparison)
  meant the review found nothing and took 5 minutes instead of 25. That is the same lesson TKT-119's
  retro reached from the other direction, now with a number attached.
- **The one thing I did not check, the reviewer did**: catalog's festival and seated payload variants.
  I verified the four subject constants `knownSchemas` keys on; the variants are separate code paths
  in the same file. A cheap "grep the whole producer file, not the constants" would have closed it.

**(2) What should the humans change?**

- **Gate 4 recommendation, fifth instance.** This ticket carved an exception into a decision made
  hours earlier (TKT-122's shutdown preference) and shipped a check that would have been an outage
  had one grep gone the other way. Both are recorded and both are correct; both are exactly what a
  PO gate exists to weigh. Five tickets, five instances — I would act on this.
- **The measurable finding of this experiment is now clear enough to state.** Across five tickets,
  `agent:coding` has been consistently the *smaller* cost, and review time tracks almost perfectly
  with how much the implementer verified before handing over. If the goal is evaluating AI-assisted
  development, the lever is not code generation speed — it is whether the implementer checks its own
  load-bearing claims, which is cheap and which it does not do reliably without being told to.
- **`docs/learnings/` is now 8 entries and growing ~1/ticket.** Worth deciding whether it stays flat
  or gets an index by theme (evidence/contracts/tests/lifecycle) before it becomes unnavigable. Not
  filed as a ticket — it is a judgement about the repo's own documentation, and it is the owner's.

**Interactive follow-up:** no new appliable skill patches from this ticket (the one gap was an
existing rule I failed to apply). The seven items from TKT-116/117/119/122 still stand.
